items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the play 'The Book that Saved the Earth', and answer.

"KING ZORB (studying a comic book upside down): Aha! This is a map of the Earth's secret weapons!
ADVISER PIP (timidly): Your Majesty, I believe it is a story about a boy and his dog.
KING ZORB: Silence! Only a genius like me can see the hidden meaning. (He turns the page and gasps.) A dog that flies! Prepare the spaceships – we must leave at once!"

What does King Zorb's reaction show about him?
items.answer: He is arrogant and foolish, misreading a simple book as a threat.
items.markingKey: He is arrogant and foolish, misreading a simple book as a threat. (1–2 marks for a complete answer.)

items.stem: Why do you think the playwright chose nursery rhymes as the book? Answer in about 40 words.
items.answer: Comic contrast between simple rhymes and alien panic; satire on pretended intelligence.

items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the play 'The Book that Saved the Earth', and answer.

"In the year 2450, the old library was the only building left standing in the city. Historians called it the most important place on the planet. Its shelves held comics, cookery books, poems and children's rhymes – and it was one of these rhymes, they said, that had frightened away the invaders three centuries before."

Why did historians call it the most important place?
